steps.name: Sample structure QC and matrix preparation
caveats: A sample with a library size several times below the median must be inspected and reported, not silently deleted — removal is a judgment that requires a stated reason
TPM values are not comparable across library protocols; if anything in the metadata hints at more than one protocol, flag it, though the profile records a single batch
With 12,000 genes the table is likely already pre-filtered by the core, so the >=1 TPM filter may remove few genes — report the count either way
steps.context: Only a gene-level TPM table was delivered — no raw counts, no Salmon quantification directories. TPM is already normalized within each sample for length and depth, so the log transform is the only transform applied; count-model normalizations (size factors, TMM) and count-model transforms (VST, rlog) are invalid here. sample_01 was sequenced at about a quarter of the median depth: TPM rescaling hides that in the column sums but not in the per-gene variance or in the number of genes detected above zero.
steps.question: Do the 12 melanoma biopsies (6 anti-PD-1 treated, 6 untreated) separate by condition on log2(TPM+1), and does the low-depth sample_01 behave as an outlier?

grounding.reason: TPM input with a low-depth sample: QC on log2(TPM+1) with PCA and sample distances (R-0071), sample_01 kept and reported rather than dropped (R-0008, R-0030), >=1 TPM in smallest-group-size filter (R-0072), log transform as the only normalization (R-0073).

constraints: Transform for QC is log2(TPM+1) — do not apply VST, rlog, TMM, or DESeq2 size factors to a TPM table
Low-abundance filter: TPM >= 1 in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size); state the floor and the number of genes kept
Keep the linear (untransformed) TPM matrix intact and unfiltered as a separate artifact for the deconvolution step
Keep sample_01 through QC; report its library-depth evidence rather than removing it
PCA on the top 500 most variable genes
steps.description: Load /eval-eight-arms-with-deconvolution-tpm-n6-1/data/inputs/abundance/tpm.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples) and /eval-eight-arms-with-deconvolution-tpm-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, sample id + condition). Verify sample ids match between the two files and that the condition column has exactly 6 treated and 6 control. Produce two matrices for downstream use and write both to disk: (a) LINEAR TPM, all 12,000 genes, no filtering, no transform — this is what the deconvolution methods consume; (b) log2(TPM+1) restricted to genes with TPM >= 1 in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size) — this is what QC and per-sample signature scoring consume. On matrix (b): PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, per-sample detected-gene counts (TPM > 0 and TPM >= 1), and the per-sample TPM sum as a sanity check that each column sums to ~1e6. Colour every plot by condition and annotate sample_01. Report where sample_01 sits on the PCA and on the distance heatmap alongside its detected-gene count relative to the other 11. Do NOT drop it — carry all 12 samples forward and record its position so downstream steps can run the sensitivity check.
acceptance_criteria: Sample ids in tpm.csv and metadata.csv reconcile 1:1; the condition column is confirmed as 6 treated vs 6 control and the exact level labels used in the files are reported verbatim
A linear-TPM matrix (12,000 x 12, unfiltered) and a log2(TPM+1) filtered matrix are both written to disk with the number of genes retained by the >=1 TPM in >=6 samples filter stated
PCA (500 most variable genes) and a sample distance heatmap are produced from the log matrix, coloured by condition, with sample_01 labelled
Per-sample detected-gene counts and TPM column sums are tabulated for all 12 samples, with sample_01's values reported explicitly beside the other 11
All 12 samples are carried forward; no sample is removed

steps.name: Multi-method immune and stromal deconvolution per sample
caveats: An enrichment score (xCell, ConsensusTME) is not a proportion: scores of different cell types are not comparable to each other and do not sum to one
Spillover between closely related cell types (e.g. CD4 vs CD8 T cells, monocyte vs macrophage) persists after compensation
sample_01's low sequencing depth increases the variance of its expression estimates and can bias rank-based scores such as xCell; flag its estimates in the table
A 12,000-gene table may be a subset of the transcriptome; low signature-gene overlap for any method is a reason to down-weight that method's estimates
steps.context: Melanoma biopsy, human, linear TPM from Salmon. The reference profiles behind EPIC and quanTIseq derive from blood and tumor-infiltrating immune cells, which is a reasonable but not exact match for a melanoma biopsy — the tissue/reference match must be stated. CIBERSORT and CIBERSORTx (LM22 proportions) are distributed under licence via a web portal and are not installed here; ESTIMATE (tumor purity, stromal and immune scores) is also absent. Do not present any substitute result as an LM22 or an ESTIMATE result.
steps.question: What is the immune and stromal cell composition of each of the 12 melanoma biopsies, estimated from the linear TPM matrix?

grounding.reason: Linear human TPM with a matched tissue: EPIC/quanTIseq for absolute fractions (R-0127), xCell for 64 enrichment scores (R-0126), all through the immunedeconv interface (R-0128); ESTIMATE absent so ConsensusTME stands in for the microenvironment and no purity is claimed (R-0130); CIBERSORT/LM22 absent (R-0131).

constraints: Input is LINEAR TPM (not logged, not z-scored) — the deconvolution methods expect the untransformed scale
Use the unfiltered 12,000-gene matrix, not the >=1 TPM filtered one: the signature matrices need their full gene sets
Run the methods through the immunedeconv interface so the outputs share one schema
ConsensusTME must be called with an explicit cancer type; use SKCM (skin cutaneous melanoma) and name it in the output
Do not claim a tumor purity — ESTIMATE is absent. Report EPIC's uncharacterized fraction as the uncharacterized fraction and xCell's immune/stroma scores as relative stand-ins, naming them as such
Do not label any output as LM22 or CIBERSORT proportions — CIBERSORT is absent
steps.description: Run deconvolution on the unfiltered LINEAR TPM matrix from T1S1 through the immunedeconv common interface, producing one long table of method x cell type x sample. Methods to run: EPIC (absolute fractions with an uncharacterized fraction, the primary estimate), quanTIseq (absolute fractions of its ten TIL10 immune types), MCP-counter (abundance scores for immune and stromal populations including fibroblasts and endothelial cells), xCell (64 cell-type enrichment scores with spillover compensation), and ConsensusTME with the melanoma cancer type (SKCM) for its 18 microenvironment populations. Report the per-sample composition as a heatmap and a stacked bar chart for the fraction-based methods, and record for each method which gene-symbol overlap it achieved against the 12,000-gene matrix — a signature gene absent from the table changes the estimate. State explicitly in the output which methods return absolute fractions (EPIC, quanTIseq — comparable across cell types and samples), which return abundance scores (MCP-counter — comparable across samples for one cell type only), and which return enrichment scores (xCell, ConsensusTME — not proportions, do not sum to one). Report EPIC's uncharacterized fraction per sample, which in a melanoma biopsy is dominated by malignant cells, and label it as such — do NOT call it a tumor purity estimate.
acceptance_criteria: A long table of method x cell type x sample covering all 12 samples for every method that ran successfully, written to disk
EPIC and quanTIseq fractions per sample sum to 1 including the uncharacterized/other fraction; this is verified numerically and reported
Per-method signature-gene overlap against the 12,000-gene TPM matrix is reported as a count and a percentage
Per-sample composition heatmap and stacked bar chart produced for the fraction-based methods
The nature of each method's output (absolute fraction vs abundance score vs enrichment score) is stated explicitly in the output text, and the reference-tissue match for a melanoma biopsy is stated
Any method that fails to run is reported by name with its error, and the remaining methods proceed

steps.name: Treated vs control composition comparison with cross-method consensus
caveats: 6 vs 6 is small: confidence intervals will be wide and a null result is uninformative about small or moderate composition shifts
xCell and ConsensusTME scores are enrichment scores, so a between-arm difference in such a score is a relative statement about that one cell type across samples, not a change in a proportion
Methods will disagree for some cell types — that disagreement is the finding for those types, not a reason to pick the method with the smallest p-value

Treated and untreated biopsies may differ in malignant-cell content, which shifts every immune fraction in an absolute-fraction method; read EPIC's uncharacterized fraction beside the immune fractions before interpreting
steps.context: This is the arm-comparison half of the research question. The design is 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, so the model needs no covariate. The composition estimates are the outcome here — they are not being used as a covariate for a gene-level model, and no gene-level differential expression is part of this plan.
steps.question: Does any immune or stromal cell type differ in abundance between the 6 anti-PD-1 treated and the 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, consistently across deconvolution methods?

grounding.reason: Consensus across two or more methods before a composition claim (R-0128); the composition estimate is reported as the outcome with its role stated (R-0132); a per-sample score compared between groups is tested with limma/t-test on the scores with BH across the tested types (R-0134); explicit reference level and named contrast (R-0036).

constraints: The test unit is the sample (6 vs 6), never the gene — do not run a gene-level test here
BH adjustment across the cell types tested within each method; state the count
Set the condition reference level explicitly to the untreated/control level; do not rely on alphabetical ordering
A composition difference is claimed only when two or more methods agree on the direction; single-method differences are reported as non-robust
Report the composition estimates as the outcome of this analysis, and state that role explicitly
Re-run the comparison with sample_01 excluded and report both results
steps.description: Take the long method x cell type x sample table from T2S1 and test the anti-PD-1 treated versus untreated contrast for each cell type within each method. The unit of inference is the sample: one value per sample per cell type, 6 vs 6, unpaired. Fit a linear model per cell type with condition as the only term (equivalently a two-sample t-test) and adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg across the cell types tested within each method; report the number of cell types tested per method. Set the reference level explicitly to the untreated/control level so a positive effect means higher abundance in the anti-PD-1 treated arm, and name the contrast as condition: treated vs control. Report per cell type the mean in each arm, the difference with a 95% confidence interval, the raw and adjusted p-value, and a boxplot with the individual sample points overlaid. Then build the consensus table: mark a cell type as a robust composition difference only when two or more methods agree on the direction of the difference, and present the per-method estimates side by side including where they disagree. Run the whole comparison a second time with sample_01 excluded and report which, if any, conclusions change. Close with an explicit power statement: with 6 vs 6 only large composition shifts are detectable, a non-significant cell type is not evidence of no difference, and the deconvolution estimates carry their own error which these tests do not propagate.
acceptance_criteria: A results table per method: cell type, mean in treated, mean in control, difference with 95% CI, raw p, BH-adjusted p, and the number of cell types tested
The reference level is the untreated/control arm and the contrast is stated as treated vs control, so the sign of every effect is unambiguous
A consensus table marking each cell type by how many methods agree on the direction of change, with the per-method estimates side by side
Boxplots per cell type with the 12 individual sample points shown, split by arm
A sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01, with a statement of which conclusions changed and which held
An explicit statement of the power limitation at n=6 per arm and of the fact that deconvolution estimation error is not propagated into these tests

steps.name: Marker-based immune and stromal signature scores per sample
caveats: A marker of a cell type in one tissue is not necessarily a marker of that cell type in another tissue; these are being applied to melanoma biopsies and that must be stated
With n=6 per arm the same power limits as T2S2 apply
Divergence between a marker score and a deconvolution fraction for the same cell type is a real result — report it rather than reconciling it by choosing one
The 12,000-gene table may not contain every marker gene; a truncated signature is a different signature
steps.context: UCell ranks genes within each sample, so its score does not depend on the other samples or on library depth — which makes it the right independent check on sample_01 and on the reference-profile deconvolvers, whose signature matrices come from a fixed external reference. A marker score is a relative enrichment, not a fraction. Human marker/gating signature collections for tumour-microenvironment populations and human pathway gene sets are present in the reference store; the executing agent must resolve them there rather than assume a filename. If a needed marker collection turns out to be absent at run time, report which signatures could not be scored and proceed with the rest — this step enriches the deconvolution answer but T2S1/T2S2 carry the research question on their own.
steps.question: Do independent rank-based marker signature scores for immune and stromal populations reproduce the deconvolution picture across the 12 samples and the treated vs control contrast?

grounding.reason: Rank-based per-sample scoring with UCell so the score does not depend on sample depth (R-0133); scores compared between groups with limma/t-test and BH across signatures, with the signature source and genes-present stated (R-0134); marker sets taken from a human cell-type marker resource with species and tissue stated (R-0135). Knowledge check warned that preprocessing_scope was unstated; it is now stated on the step — no classifier is fitted, so fold-internal preprocessing does not apply.

constraints: Score on the log2(TPM+1) filtered matrix, not on linear TPM
Use human marker sets only — this is a human melanoma biopsy; a mouse or rat set here produces confident nonsense
Resolve marker and pathway gene sets against the reference data actually present in the environment; verify presence before use and report what was used
State the marker source, its version, and the count of signature genes present in the matrix for every signature
Report the scores as relative enrichments, never as cell fractions
Report a signature score as descriptive whenever fewer than about half its marker genes are present in the matrix

Preprocessing scope: the filter and any scaling are applied once to the whole matrix here because this is a scoring and two-group testing step, not a trained classifier — no cross-validated model is fitted, so no fold-internal preprocessing applies; state this in the output
steps.description: Score each of the 12 samples with UCell (rank-based, Mann-Whitney U on the within-sample gene ranks) on the log2(TPM+1) filtered matrix from T1S1, using marker sets for the immune and stromal populations of a tumour microenvironment: CD8 T cells, CD4 T cells, regulatory T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, neutrophils, mast cells, plasma cells, fibroblasts/CAF, endothelial cells, plus a cytotoxicity signature and an interferon-gamma response signature. Resolve the marker sets from the reference data the environment actually holds — human cell-type marker/gating signature collections and human pathway gene sets are present in the reference store; use human sets only and state the source, its version, and the number of signature genes present in the 12,000-gene matrix for every signature scored. A signature whose genes are largely missing from the matrix is a different signature and must be flagged or dropped with the count reported. Then test each score for the treated vs control contrast exactly as in T2S2: limma (or a two-sample t-test) on the per-sample scores with the control arm as reference, BH adjustment across the signatures tested, effect size with a 95% CI, and boxplots with individual points. Finally, correlate each signature score against the corresponding cell-type estimate from T2S1 across the 12 samples (Spearman) and report where the marker-based and reference-profile-based routes agree and where they diverge.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample score matrix (signatures x 12 samples) written to disk
For every signature: its source collection, that collection's version, the number of genes in the signature, and the number present in the 12,000-gene matrix
A treated vs control test per signature with the control arm as reference, BH-adjusted across signatures, with effect sizes and 95% CIs and boxplots showing the 12 individual samples
Spearman correlations between each marker score and the matching cell-type estimate from T2S1 across the 12 samples, with agreements and divergences named
Any signature that could not be scored because its markers are absent from the reference store or from the matrix is listed by name with the reason

steps.name: Composition report and reproducibility record
caveats: A composition difference between arms in an absolute-fraction method can arise from a change in malignant-cell content rather than from a change in immune infiltration; read the uncharacterized fraction alongside
This is an observational comparison of treated and untreated biopsies with n=6 per arm — it does not establish that anti-PD-1 caused any composition difference observed
steps.context: The audience asked two things: the composition of every sample, and whether it differs between arms. Both are answered here. Only a TPM table was available, which constrains the method set and is stated up front rather than buried.
steps.question: What is the per-sample immune and stromal composition of the 12 melanoma biopsies, and which composition differences between anti-PD-1 treated and untreated samples are supported by more than one method?

grounding.reason: Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and pinned collection versions in the report (R-0086); the composition estimate is reported with its role as the outcome stated (R-0132).

constraints: Report the composition first and the statistics second; do not lead with p-values
State every method's output nature (absolute fraction, abundance score, enrichment score) wherever its numbers appear
Do not upgrade a single-method difference into a finding
Store the reproducibility record with the results
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T2S1, T2S2 and T3S1. It contains: (1) the QC summary including sample_01's depth evidence and its position on the PCA and distance heatmap; (2) the per-sample composition table and figures for all 12 samples, method by method, with the nature of each method's output stated; (3) the treated vs control comparison with effect sizes, confidence intervals and BH-adjusted p-values, and the cross-method consensus table naming which cell types are supported by two or more methods and which are single-method or contradictory; (4) the marker-score results beside the deconvolution results with their concordance; (5) the sample_01 sensitivity result; (6) an explicit limitations section covering the n=6-per-arm power limit, the absence of raw counts, the absence of CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE and what was used in their place, the reference-tissue match of each method to a melanoma biopsy, and the fact that deconvolution error is not propagated into the between-arm tests; (7) the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seed of every step that used randomness, every package version, and the version of every marker/pathway collection used. Lead the report with what the composition actually is and which differences survived the consensus requirement — not with a p-value list.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample composition table covering all 12 samples is presented, with each method's output type labelled
The treated vs control results are presented with effect sizes, 95% CIs and BH-adjusted p-values, and the consensus table separates multi-method-supported differences from single-method ones

A limitations section explicitly covers: n=6 per arm, TPM-only input with no raw counts, CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE absence and their substitutes, reference-tissue match, and unpropagated deconvolution error
The sample_01 sensitivity result is reported
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and marker/pathway collection versions is stored with the results, not in a separate note
No claim of tumor purity and no claim labelled as LM22 proportions appears anywhere in the report

plan.title: Melanoma TPM immune/stromal deconvolution: anti-PD-1 vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The core delivered a gene-level TPM table only (/data/inputs/abundance/tpm.csv, 12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples from Salmon) plus a 12-row metadata table with a single `condition` column (6 anti-PD-1 treated vs 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, unpaired, single batch). The question is per-sample immune and stromal composition and whether it differs between the two arms — a deconvolution question, not a differential-expression question, so no gene-level DE or enrichment step is planned.

The data state dictates the methods. TPM is not counts: DESeq2/edgeR/voom are excluded, log2(TPM+1) is the only transform, and no TMM or size-factor normalization is applied. Deconvolution methods, however, want LINEAR TPM — so the pipeline keeps two matrices in parallel: linear TPM (unfiltered, for EPIC/quanTIseq/ConsensusTME/xCell, which expect the full transcriptome) and log2(TPM+1) after a >=1 TPM in >=6 samples filter (for QC, marker-signature scoring, and the linear models on scores).

T1S1 is sample-structure QC on the log matrix. It matters here specifically: sample_01 was sequenced at roughly a quarter of the median depth. TPM is depth-normalized within a sample, so a shallow library does not shift the scale but it does raise per-gene variance and depress the count of detected genes, which is exactly what rank-based deconvolution scores are sensitive to. sample_01 is kept, plotted, and reported, not silently dropped; every downstream composition claim is re-checked with it excluded as a sensitivity analysis.

T2S1 runs the deconvolution itself through the immunedeconv interface with several methods on the same linear TPM matrix: EPIC and quanTIseq for absolute fractions with an uncharacterized (tumor) fraction, MCP-counter for between-sample abundance scores, xCell for 64 enrichment scores, ConsensusTME with the SKCM cancer type for a melanoma-matched microenvironment estimate. No single method wins for every cell type, so the per-sample composition table is reported method by method and the between-arm claims in T2S2 require agreement in direction from two or more methods. CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE are licensed/absent — no LM22 proportion and no tumor-purity number is claimed; EPIC's uncharacterized fraction and xCell's immune/stroma scores are reported as relative stand-ins with that caveat stated.

T2S2 tests the arm difference. With n=6 per arm the unit of inference is the sample, not the gene: one value per sample per cell type, a two-group unpaired test per cell type, BH across cell types within each method. Six versus six detects only large composition shifts; the step reports effect sizes with confidence intervals and states the power limit rather than reading a p-value list as a finding.

T3S1 is the orthogonal marker-based route: rank-based per-sample scores (UCell) for immune and stromal signatures, which do not depend on a reference profile matrix and so fail differently from the least-squares deconvolvers. Agreement between a fraction estimate and an independent marker score is the strongest evidence available from a 12-sample TPM table; disagreement is reported as such.

T4S1 assembles the per-sample composition matrix, the between-arm comparison, the cross-method concordance, the sample_01 sensitivity result, and the reproducibility record.

steps.method: Sample structure QC on log2(TPM+1): PCA, sample distance heatmap, detected genes
log2(TPM+1) only, no count-based between-sample normalization
EPIC absolute cell fractions from TPM with uncharacterized fraction, plus quanTIseq, MCP-counter, xCell and ConsensusTME through immunedeconv for consensus
UCell rank-based per-sample immune/stromal marker signature scores, tested with limma on the scores

Do not present any substitute result as an LM22 or an ESTIMATE result.

steps.name: Treated vs control composition comparison with cross-method consensus
steps.question: Does any immune or stromal cell type differ in abundance between the 6 anti-PD-1 treated and the 6 untreated melanoma biopsies, consistently across deconvolution methods?
steps.description: Take the long method x cell type x sample table from T2S1 and test the anti-PD-1 treated versus untreated contrast for each cell type within each method. The unit of inference is the sample: one value per sample per cell type, 6 vs 6, unpaired. Fit a linear model per cell type with condition as the only term (equivalently a two-sample t-test) and adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg across the cell types tested within each method; report the number of cell types tested per method. Set the reference level explicitly to the untreated/control level so a positive effect means higher abundance in the anti-PD-1 treated arm, and name the contrast as condition: treated vs control. Report per cell type the mean in each arm, the difference with a 95% confidence interval, the raw and adjusted p-value, and a boxplot with the individual sample points overlaid. Then build the consensus table: mark a cell type as a robust composition difference only when two or more methods agree on the direction of the difference, and present the per-method estimates side by side including where they disagree. Run the whole comparison a second time with sample_01 excluded and report which, if any, conclusions change. Close with an explicit power statement: with 6 vs 6 only large composition shifts are detectable, a non-significant cell type is not evidence of no difference, and the deconvolution estimates carry their own error which these tests do not propagate.
steps.context: This is the arm-comparison half of the research question. The design is 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, so the model needs no covariate. The composition estimates are the outcome here — they are not being used as a covariate for a gene-level model, and no gene-level differential expression is part of this plan.
acceptance_criteria: A results table per method: cell type, mean in treated, mean in control, difference with 95% CI, raw p, BH-adjusted p, and the number of cell types tested
The reference level is the untreated/control arm and the contrast is stated as treated vs control, so the sign of every effect is unambiguous
A consensus table marking each cell type by how many methods agree on the direction of change, with the per-method estimates side by side
Boxplots per cell type with the 12 individual sample points shown, split by arm
A sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01, with a statement of which conclusions changed and which held
An explicit statement of the power limitation at n=6 per arm and of the fact that deconvolution estimation error is not propagated into these tests
constraints: The test unit is the sample (6 vs 6), never the gene — do not run a gene-level test here
BH adjustment across the cell types tested within each method; state the count
Set the condition reference level explicitly to the untreated/control level; do not rely on alphabetical ordering
A composition difference is claimed only when two or more methods agree on the direction; single-method differences are reported as non-robust
Report the composition estimates as the outcome of this analysis, and state that role explicitly
Re-run the comparison with sample_01 excluded and report both results
caveats: 6 vs 6 is small: confidence intervals will be wide and a null result is uninformative about small or moderate composition shifts
xCell and ConsensusTME scores are enrichment scores, so a between-arm difference in such a score is a relative statement about that one cell type across samples, not a change in a proportion
Methods will disagree for some cell types — that disagreement is the finding for those types, not a reason to pick the method with the smallest p-value

Treated and untreated biopsies may differ in malignant-cell content, which shifts every immune fraction in an absolute-fraction method; read EPIC's uncharacterized fraction beside the immune fractions before interpreting

grounding.reason: Consensus across two or more methods before a composition claim (R-0128); the composition estimate is reported as the outcome with its role stated (R-0132); a per-sample score compared between groups is tested with limma/t-test on the scores with BH across the tested types (R-0134); explicit reference level and named contrast (R-0036).

steps.name: Marker-based immune and stromal signature scores per sample
steps.question: Do independent rank-based marker signature scores for immune and stromal populations reproduce the deconvolution picture across the 12 samples and the treated vs control contrast?
steps.description: Score each of the 12 samples with UCell (rank-based, Mann-Whitney U on the within-sample gene ranks) on the log2(TPM+1) filtered matrix from T1S1, using marker sets for the immune and stromal populations of a tumour microenvironment: CD8 T cells, CD4 T cells, regulatory T cells, B cells, NK cells, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, neutrophils, mast cells, plasma cells, fibroblasts/CAF, endothelial cells, plus a cytotoxicity signature and an interferon-gamma response signature. Resolve the marker sets from the reference data the environment actually holds — human cell-type marker/gating signature collections and human pathway gene sets are present in the reference store; use human sets only and state the source, its version, and the number of signature genes present in the 12,000-gene matrix for every signature scored. A signature whose genes are largely missing from the matrix is a different signature and must be flagged or dropped with the count reported. Then test each score for the treated vs control contrast exactly as in T2S2: limma (or a two-sample t-test) on the per-sample scores with the control arm as reference, BH adjustment across the signatures tested, effect size with a 95% CI, and boxplots with individual points. Finally, correlate each signature score against the corresponding cell-type estimate from T2S1 across the 12 samples (Spearman) and report where the marker-based and reference-profile-based routes agree and where they diverge.
steps.context: UCell ranks genes within each sample, so its score does not depend on the other samples or on library depth — which makes it the right independent check on sample_01 and on the reference-profile deconvolvers, whose signature matrices come from a fixed external reference. A marker score is a relative enrichment, not a fraction. Human marker/gating signature collections for tumour-microenvironment populations and human pathway gene sets are present in the reference store; the executing agent must resolve them there rather than assume a filename. If a needed marker collection turns out to be absent at run time, report which signatures could not be scored and proceed with the rest — this step enriches the deconvolution answer but T2S1/T2S2 carry the research question on their own.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample score matrix (signatures x 12 samples) written to disk
For every signature: its source collection, that collection's version, the number of genes in the signature, and the number present in the 12,000-gene matrix
A treated vs control test per signature with the control arm as reference, BH-adjusted across signatures, with effect sizes and 95% CIs and boxplots showing the 12 individual samples
Spearman correlations between each marker score and the matching cell-type estimate from T2S1 across the 12 samples, with agreements and divergences named
Any signature that could not be scored because its markers are absent from the reference store or from the matrix is listed by name with the reason
constraints: Score on the log2(TPM+1) filtered matrix, not on linear TPM
Use human marker sets only — this is a human melanoma biopsy; a mouse or rat set here produces confident nonsense
Resolve marker and pathway gene sets against the reference data actually present in the environment; verify presence before use and report what was used
State the marker source, its version, and the count of signature genes present in the matrix for every signature
Report the scores as relative enrichments, never as cell fractions
Report a signature score as descriptive whenever fewer than about half its marker genes are present in the matrix

Preprocessing scope: the filter and any scaling are applied once to the whole matrix here because this is a scoring and two-group testing step, not a trained classifier — no cross-validated model is fitted, so no fold-internal preprocessing applies; state this in the output
caveats: A marker of a cell type in one tissue is not necessarily a marker of that cell type in another tissue; these are being applied to melanoma biopsies and that must be stated
With n=6 per arm the same power limits as T2S2 apply
Divergence between a marker score and a deconvolution fraction for the same cell type is a real result — report it rather than reconciling it by choosing one
The 12,000-gene table may not contain every marker gene; a truncated signature is a different signature

grounding.reason: Rank-based per-sample scoring with UCell so the score does not depend on sample depth (R-0133); scores compared between groups with limma/t-test and BH across signatures, with the signature source and genes-present stated (R-0134); marker sets taken from a human cell-type marker resource with species and tissue stated (R-0135). Knowledge check warned that preprocessing_scope was unstated; it is now stated on the step — no classifier is fitted, so fold-internal preprocessing does not apply.

steps.name: Composition report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the per-sample immune and stromal composition of the 12 melanoma biopsies, and which composition differences between anti-PD-1 treated and untreated samples are supported by more than one method?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T2S1, T2S2 and T3S1. It contains: (1) the QC summary including sample_01's depth evidence and its position on the PCA and distance heatmap; (2) the per-sample composition table and figures for all 12 samples, method by method, with the nature of each method's output stated; (3) the treated vs control comparison with effect sizes, confidence intervals and BH-adjusted p-values, and the cross-method consensus table naming which cell types are supported by two or more methods and which are single-method or contradictory; (4) the marker-score results beside the deconvolution results with their concordance; (5) the sample_01 sensitivity result; (6) an explicit limitations section covering the n=6-per-arm power limit, the absence of raw counts, the absence of CIBERSORT/LM22 and ESTIMATE and what was used in their place, the reference-tissue match of each method to a melanoma biopsy, and the fact that deconvolution error is not propagated into the between-arm tests; (7) the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, the random seed of every step that used randomness, every package version, and the version of every marker/pathway collection used. Lead the report with what the composition actually is and which differences survived the consensus requirement — not with a p-value list.
steps.context: The audience asked two things: the composition of every sample, and whether it differs between arms. Both are answered here. Only a TPM table was available, which constrains the method set and is stated up front rather than buried.

No claim of tumor purity and no claim labelled as LM22 proportions appears anywhere in the report
constraints: Report the composition first and the statistics second; do not lead with p-values
State every method's output nature (absolute fraction, abundance score, enrichment score) wherever its numbers appear
Do not upgrade a single-method difference into a finding
Store the reproducibility record with the results
